poolEstimate.denominator: eligible active visible generals with numeric maxHp
poolEstimate.note: Estimated from the registered new_heg_mode general pool; not an observed match rate.

observedMatches.note: Current sanitized evidence records decisions and shapes, not per-skill activation counts.

priority.rationale: Pindian win unlocks an extra/unlimited-distance/additional-target Slash; loss disables Slash for the turn.
Two pool occurrences; target and follow-up branch determine public information and optional enemy discard.
Two pool occurrences; target choice trades an enemy discard against a forced Slash response.
Card advantage plus a Slash residue at the cost of HP; lethal/low-HP timing must be rejected.
Frequent Slash/Jink conversion plus delayed damage/recovery choice; requires play and response-path parity.
Two-card multi-target attack with per-suit phase cost; needs exhaustive suit/card and target evaluation.
Direct damage with a choice between one HP and a weapon; faction-aware target and cost comparison are missing.
Flexible Slash conversion and Diamond distance bypass; target/resource policy must preserve response legality.
Core hand-quality conversion; card count and discard quality determine whether the draw exchange is positive.
Top-deck response choice preserves the lower-keep-value legal basic card and consumes only server-exposed candidates.
Once-per-turn target conversion avoids low-HP activation, prefers the smallest hostile public hand, and discards the highest-value visible card in the no-Slash branch.
Two-target hand exchange selects an ally/enemy pair where the enemy has more public cards and pays the difference with the cheapest legal cards.
Red-card Fire Attack conversion; response/target and card conservation policy need a dedicated view-as test.
Peach response conversion can change survival; requires dying/response fixtures and no private-information shortcut.
Nullification timing is high impact but must use the existing contextual response evaluator, not a blind play strategy.
Hand-to-Slash conversion targets a friendly non-empty hand and reveals a card from the smallest visible category to maximize converted cards.
Limited general-sacrifice timing prefers a living same-faction ally who can use Yongjue and receive two cards, with self as a safe fallback.
Black-card conversion evaluates low-keep-value prefixes under the phase cap and activates only for a positive simulated draw exchange.
